There were no commits after the existing draft, so I corrected `docs/changelog-draft.md` instead of rewriting it. Nothing is published or committed.

The draft already covered all 11 commits, from the project scaffold on 2026-09-03 to the sort-comparator caching on 2026-09-10. Its headings, breaking-change-first order and plain wording were already right. I changed two things:

- **Config move:** The draft told upgraders to copy `config/app.toml.example`, which doesn't exist in the repo. It now says to move settings from `.apprc` into `config/app.toml`, which ships with `port = 3000` under `[server]`.
- **CSV export:** I added "Added CSV export", which the draft left out even though it was a new feature in the range.

The draft's header still says "This is the first draft". That is true, since git has no earlier changelog commit.

`docs/setup.md` step 2 has the same bug the draft had. It says to copy `config/app.toml.example`, which was never added. That edit came in the commit that moved the config, so a new user following the guide hits a missing file. I left it because the file is outside the changelog task. The fix is to either delete step 2, because `config/app.toml` is already committed, or add the example file. Which should it be?
